findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional frequency-counted sliding window. Its k-zero guard is explicit, left and right have their standard meanings, zero-count deletion preserves exact distinctness, and the best-length update follows restoration of validity. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 340 and its Python lengthOfLongestSubstringKDistinct surface. The Reference preserves contiguous-substring semantics, the at-most-k distinct limit, maximum length result, both explained source examples, and both constraints including k=0.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064485337. Its guard, frequency updates, shrink loop, zero-count deletion, left advance, and best update structurally align with the protected app-local source; only the required class wrapper and the app-local dict annotation differ.

The legal fully valid alternating tiers use 16, 64, and 256 characters, span 16x, and prevent early termination or shrinking. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.02 relative growth and 1.05x; correct restart-from-each-left scanning passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +1.23 and 93.55x.

The Approach exactly explains window maintenance, frequency-based deletion, minimal feasible left boundary, endpoint and global optimality arguments, O(n) time, and O(k) space. It now limits boundary discussion to legal nonempty strings instead of claiming an out-of-contract empty input.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples and explanations in order, both constraints, contiguous semantics, and the at-most distinctness boundary.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact strings, distinct limits, and longest lengths.
The invented k-zero row is now a trial rather than a source sample, and the illegal empty-string trial was removed because the source requires at least one character.

The one-character k-zero trial covers the minimum string length and minimum k; a 26-distinct-character row uses the maximum k of 50, and a legal 50,000-character alternating string was verified outside cases.json.
Prefix, suffix, interior, and whole-string optima cover every window position, while repeated copies and several evictions exercise frequency-aware shrinking.
A fewer-than-k whole-string trial distinguishes the at-most contract from an exactly-k interpretation.
A quadratic start/end oracle verified all eight authored results; the target also matched it on 16,395 exhaustive strings of lengths one through seven over {a, b, c} with k from zero through four.
All eight correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 16-, 64-, and 256-character alternating workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
